Each such file must (a) be syntactically valid TypeScript, (b) contain at least one `it()` or `test()` call that is not inside a `.skip` block, and (c) not consist solely of type-import statements with no runtime assertions. Each test file is counted under exactly one layer (no double-counting). GATE-ERROR-HANDLING + GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR: Every outbound API call is enclosed in a try/catch (or equivalent .catch()) block. Non-2xx responses from upstream are surfaced as a JSON body `{ "error": string, "status": number }` with a matching HTTP status code; the original upstream 4xx–5xx status code must be preserved; if the upstream returns a status outside 400–599 (e.g. 1xx, 3xx without redirect-following, or a network-level error including connection timeout, DNS failure, or ECONNREFUSED) the server must respond with HTTP 502. stories.description: Second half of the Skyscanner mini-app code review. The agent reads the partially-populated review document produced by SKY-006-A and performs deep inspection of security (API key exposure and query-parameter validation), error handling (missing-param 400 responses and upstream error propagation), and Express static-file safety (path traversal prevention). It then writes the `## Verdict` section and finalises the document. This story depends on SKY-006-A being complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Dependency-guard precondition: Before performing any category check, the agent MUST verify that `/home/bradleyjerome/projects/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` exists and contains ALL of the following H2 headings produced by SKY-006-A: `## TypeScript`, `## Tests`, `## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`. These heading names are the authoritative list inlined here — no cross-story AC reference is required. If the file is absent, empty, or missing any of these headings, the agent MUST abort with a non-zero exit code and emit a human-readable error message identifying the missing prerequisite; it MUST NOT create a partial or blank review document in this failure mode.

Security check — API key exposure: The agent MUST determine the exact string value assigned to the API key (from environment variable, config constant, or .env file under /home/bradleyjerome/projects/skyscanner-app) and perform a case-insensitive literal grep for that value across: (a) all files under src/, (b) the captured stdout/stderr from the `vitest run` execution, and (c) any .log files under /home/bradleyjerome/projects/skyscanner-app. Zero matches MUST be found across all three scopes; any match is a blocking Security finding. If the API key value cannot be determined (e.g. it is only read from process.env at runtime with no default), the agent MUST record this as an informational note and instead grep for the environment variable name to confirm it is never interpolated into a response body or log statement.

Security check — query parameter validation and binary file handling: Every Express route handler that accepts query parameters MUST validate each parameter before use via an explicit check (e.g. `if (!req.query.x)` or equivalent), a validation library schema (e.g. Zod, Joi, express-validator), or dedicated middleware — implicit type coercion alone is insufficient. The agent MUST enumerate all route handlers found in src/ and confirm each one validates its inputs; any route handler that uses a query parameter without prior explicit validation is a blocking Security finding. Additionally, if any route handler reads or serves files from disk, the agent MUST confirm that binary or non-UTF-8 file content is never decoded as UTF-8 text and re-emitted in an error message (which could expose partial binary data); any such path is a blocking Security finding.

Supply-chain secrets check: The agent MUST inspect the resolved contents of `node_modules/` (or, if node_modules is absent, the lockfile at `/home/bradleyjerome/projects/skyscanner-app/package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`) for any file whose name matches `*.env`, `.env*`, `config.json`, or `secrets.*` at depth ≤ 2 within any single package directory. Any match is a blocking Security finding labelled `Supply-Chain Credential Exposure`. If node_modules is absent and no lockfile exists, the agent MUST record this as an informational note and skip this check without issuing a finding.

Error Handling check — missing/invalid parameters and Content-Type enforcement: Every Express route handler that declares a required query parameter MUST return HTTP 400 with a JSON body of the shape `{ "error": "<non-empty string>" }` (additional fields are permitted) when that parameter is: (a) absent from the request, (b) present but an empty string, or (c) present but not parseable as its declared type (e.g. a non-numeric string where a number is required). The agent MUST verify this by static analysis and, where the test suite exercises these paths, by inspecting the relevant test assertions. Failure of any sub-case (a), (b), or (c) for any route is a blocking Error Handling finding. Additionally, every error response (HTTP 4xx or 5xx) with a JSON body MUST set `Content-Type: application/json` — either via `res.json(...)` (which sets it automatically in Express) or via an explicit `res.setHeader`/`res.type('json')` call before `res.send(...)`; any error response path that sends a JSON-shaped body without an explicit or implicit `application/json` Content-Type is a blocking Error Handling finding.

Error Handling check — upstream error propagation (GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR): All code paths that invoke or await the upstream Skyscanner API MUST be wrapped in try/catch or .catch() / Promise rejection handling. Non-2xx HTTP status codes returned by the upstream MUST be mapped to a JSON response of the shape `{ "error": string, "status": number }` forwarded to the Express caller with the same HTTP status code or a semantically equivalent one (e.g. 502 Bad Gateway is acceptable for a 500 upstream). No unhandled-rejection or uncaught-exception path reachable via upstream errors is permitted. The agent MUST trace every call site to the upstream API in src/ and confirm coverage; any unguarded call site or missing non-2xx mapping is a blocking Error Handling finding. Express async error handlers MUST call `next(err)` rather than swallowing the error silently (GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR).

Express Safety check — path traversal prevention and CORS: Static file serving MUST use `express.static` with a base directory derived exclusively from a fixed, hard-coded constant (e.g. `path.join(__dirname, 'public')` or `path.resolve(__dirname, '../public')`). The agent MUST grep src/ for all occurrences of: `path.join`, `path.resolve`, `readFile`, `createReadStream`, and `sendFile`, and inspect each call site; any call site that incorporates user-controlled input is a blocking Express Safety finding. Additionally (EXPRESS_CORS gate): if a CORS middleware is present, the agent MUST confirm its `origin` option is not set to `'*'` in a production configuration; a wildcard CORS origin in a non-test context is a blocking Express Safety finding.

Verdict integrity: The `## Verdict` section MUST contain exactly one line matching the POSIX ERE regex `^(PASS|FAIL)$` (case-sensitive, anchored at both start and end of line, no leading or trailing whitespace, no punctuation, no markdown formatting) as the first non-blank line of that section. stories.description: Implement `src/table.ts` exporting `renderTable(flights: FlightResult[], currency?: string): string`. The function is pure (no I/O). Column order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Dynamic width computation, left-align non-Price columns, right-align Price column, LF-joined rows, no trailing newline. Wire into existing `src/cli.ts`: pass the `FlightResult[]` from `searchFlights` and any `currency` option to `renderTable`, then write the result to stdout.
acceptanceCriteria: Header row (output line index 0) columns appear in exactly this order: `Airline`, `Price`, `Departure`, `Arrival`, `Duration`, `Stops`. Cells are joined by ` | ` (one space, pipe, one space). The row has no leading and no trailing `|`. For every non-Price column, W = `Math.max(header.length, max(value.toString().length for all rows))`. `.toString()` is called on numeric fields (`stops`, `price`, etc.) with no locale-aware formatting (`toLocaleString`, `toFixed`, thousands separators are forbidden). For the Price column each cell is formatted as `<symbol><price.toString()>` and W = `Math.max('Price'.length, max(formattedPrice.length for all rows))`; a multi-character symbol such as `'USD'` contributes its full length to W.

The separator row (output line index 1) contains exactly six dash segments, one per column in the order specified in AC1, joined by ` | ` (space-pipe-space). The row has no leading and no trailing `|`. Each dash segment is the character `-` repeated exactly W times where W is the corresponding column width computed in AC1. The separator contains no characters other than `-`, space, and `|`.
When given an empty array of flights, the returned string is exactly `No flights found.` with no leading or trailing newlines.

For non-empty input, the returned string is the header row (line index 0), the separator row (line index 1), and one data row per flight (lines index 2 through 1+flights.length), joined by `\n` (LF, U+000A — not CRLF). The string has no leading newline and no trailing newline; splitting the result by `\n` yields exactly `2 + flights.length` elements. Every row has no leading and no trailing `|`. The Price column is right-padded with spaces to its width W (right-aligned within its cell); every other column is left-padded with spaces to its width W (left-aligned within its cell). `renderTable` is a pure function and does not call `console.log`, `process.stdout.write`, `process.exit`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `fs.*`, `path.*`, `process.stdin`, or perform any I/O, network, filesystem, or global mutable state side effects.
When given a FlightResult with a null or undefined airline, the Airline column displays as an empty string.
When given a FlightResult with a null or undefined price, the Price column displays as an empty string.
When given a FlightResult with a null or undefined departure, the Departure column displays as an empty string.
When given a FlightResult with a null or undefined arrival, the Arrival column displays as an empty string.

stories.description: Implement src/server.ts containing GET /search route with validation, CORS, error handling, and flight search functionality. The route validates from/to/date/adults query params (400 on invalid input), calls client.searchFlights({ origin, destination, date, adults }), and instantiates SkyscannerClient({}) inside each route handler (per-request, never at module level).
